The first vending machine was invented almost two thousand years ago.
In the first century, a Greek engineer named Hero of Alexandria designed a machine for temples.
You dropped a bronze coin into a slot at the top.
The coin fell onto a small tray, attached to a lever.
Its weight tipped the tray, which opened a valve, and a little holy water poured out.
When the coin slid off the tray, the lever popped back up, and the water stopped.
So the next time a vending machine eats your money, remember, it's an ancient tradition.
